messages.subject: Comparison line transect and point transect
parts:
Hi there,

Aim was to find out whether point transects or line transects are more
practical in the field collecting data on bird density and abundance. We
estimated distances to the detected birds for both methods.=20
However, I am not sure if the quality of distance data is good. In fact,
distances were estimated to 5, 10, 15 etc.=20
I have alot more data from point transects than line transects. I used
DISTANCE for both methods to estimate density, but get a different result=
. I
categorised and truncated data for both analyses the same way (4 categori=
es)
and chi-square were ok, and I chose the best model with the lowest AIC.=20=


I guess the difference in result (see below) is due to different detectio=
n
probability and encounter rate? Is that a reason, or am I on a completely=

wrong track? How do I chose suitable categories, and do I have to use the=

same categories for the data of both methods?

The data was from the Cape Turtle dove, which also occur in clusters. Mea=
n
cluster size was used in the analysis, because the log against x does not=

work for categories....

I appreciate your help and guidance,

kind regards,
Johanna Reinhard

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Comparison line transect and point transect
parts:
Johanna, I think the problem is more to do with the design than the
method. You should get comparable abundance estimates - and you do,
when you take account of the very wide confidence interval for lines.
That is unsurprising, when you consider your design has just 3 lines.
That is far too few. (In the 2001 book, we say 'a minimum of 10-20
lines'.) If you can fit 72 points into your survey region, you can
certainly fit more than 3 lines in.

You should also use laser rangefinders, as measurement errors in point
transect sampling can generate substantial upward bias in the abundance
estimate - and your point transect abundance estimate is higher here
than your line transect estimate.

Steve Buckland

parts:
Hey
During=20the=20training=20we=20shortly=20toughed=20the=20problem=20of=20o=
bservation=20points
(points=20sampling)=20without=20observations,=20now=20I'm=20focussing=20t=
he=20problem=20in
reality,=20I=20do=20not=20remember=20how=20to=20enter=20the=20data=20in=
=20the=20data=20sheet

Please=20advise=20?
Jim
=20

-----Oorspronkelijk=20bericht-----
Van:=20Wildlife=20abundance=20estimation=20using=20distance=20sampling=20=
techniques.
[mailto:DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK]=20Namens=20Steve=20Buckland

Onderwerp:=20Re:=20[DIST-SAMP]=20Comparison=20line=20transect=20and=20poi=
nt=20transect

Johanna,=20I=20think=20the=20problem=20is=20more=20to=20do=20with=20the=
=20design=20than=20the
method.=20=20You=20should=20get=20comparable=20abundance=20estimates=20-=
=20and=20you=20do,
when=20you=20take=20account=20of=20the=20very=20wide=20confidence=20inter=
val=20for=20lines.=20=20
That=20is=20unsurprising,=20when=20you=20consider=20your=20design=20has=
=20just=203=20lines.=20=20
That=20is=20far=20too=20few.=20=20(In=20the=202001=20book,=20we=20say=20'=
a=20minimum=20of=2010-20
lines'.)=20=20If=20you=20can=20fit=2072=20points=20into=20your=20survey=
=20region,=20you=20can
certainly=20fit=20more=20than=203=20lines=20in.

You=20should=20also=20use=20laser=20rangefinders,=20as=20measurement=20er=
rors=20in=20point
transect=20sampling=20can=20generate=20substantial=20upward=20bias=20in=
=20the=20abundance
estimate=20-=20and=20your=20point=20transect=20abundance=20estimate=20is=
=20higher=20here
than=20your=20line=20transect=20estimate.

Steve=20Buckland

Johanna=20Reinhard=20wrote:
> >=20Hi=20there,
> >
> >=20Aim=20was=20to=20find=20out=20whether=20point=20transects=20or=20line=
=20transects=20are=20more

> >=20practical=20in=20the=20field=20collecting=20data=20on=20bird=20densit=
y=20and=20abundance.=20
> >=20We=20estimated=20distances=20to=20the=20detected=20birds=20for=20both=
=20methods.
> >=20However,=20I=20am=20not=20sure=20if=20the=20quality=20of=20distance=
=20data=20is=20good.=20In=20
> >=20fact,=20distances=20were=20estimated=20to=205,=2010,=2015=20etc.
> >=20I=20have=20alot=20more=20data=20from=20point=20transects=20than=20lin=
e=20transects.=20I=20used

> >=20DISTANCE=20for=20both=20methods=20to=20estimate=20density,=20but=20ge=
t=20a=20different=20
> >=20result.=20I=20categorised=20and=20truncated=20data=20for=20both=20ana=
lyses=20the=20same=20
> >=20way=20(4=20categories)=20and=20chi-square=20were=20ok,=20and=20I=20ch=
ose=20the=20best=20model
with=20the=20lowest=20AIC.
> >
> >=20I=20guess=20the=20difference=20in=20result=20(see=20below)=20is=20due=
=20to=20different=20
> >=20detection=20probability=20and=20encounter=20rate?=20Is=20that=20a=20r=

> >=20have=20to=20use=20the=20same=20categories=20for=20the=20data=20of=20b=
oth=20methods?
> >
> >=20The=20data=20was=20from=20the=20Cape=20Turtle=20dove,=20which=20also=
=20occur=20in=20clusters.=20
> >=20Mean=20cluster=20size=20was=20used=20in=20the=20analysis,=20because=
=20the=20log=20against=20x=20
> >=20does=20not=20work=20for=20categories....
> >
> >=20I=20appreciate=20your=20help=20and=20guidance,
